english.title: Obstructs authorised person in the exercise of a search power under s.40 - Immigration, Asylum and Nationality Act 2006
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) obstructed **(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..), a person authorised by the Secretary of State by virtue of section 40 of the Immigration, Asylum and Nationality Act 2006 in the exercise by

(A)_[him]_
(B)_[her]_

of a power to search under section 40 of the Act
english.legislation: Contrary to section 41(6)(c) and (8) of the Immigration, Asylum and Nationality Act 2006.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 41(5) of the Immigration, Asylum and Nationality Act 2006 provides that an individual delivered to an immigration officer under section 40 shall be treated as if discovered by the immigration officer on a search under Schedule 2 to the Immigration Act 1971.
(ii) Section 41(7) of the Immigration, Asylum and Nationality Act 2006 provides that a person does not commit this offence by doing or failing to do anything in respect of an authorised person who is not readily identifiable:-
(a) as a constable or officer of Revenue and Customs, or
(b) as an authorised person (whether by means of a uniform or badge or otherwise).

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: 51 weeks imprisonment and /or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Note:
Section 41(9) of the Immigration, Asylum and Nationality Act 2006 provides that in relation to a conviction occurring before the commencement of section 281(5) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003, the reference to 51 weeks shall be taken as a reference to six months.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
